content_html:
Whole raw potatoes generally store better in a cool, dark, dry, ventilated place than in the refrigerator. Cold storage can alter sugars and texture; cooked or cut potatoes follow different food-safety rules and should be refrigerated promptly.

Store whole potatoes in a cool dark place

A ventilated pantry away from sunlight, heat, and moisture helps slow sprouting and spoilage. Avoid tightly sealed plastic bags that trap condensation.

Refrigeration can change cooking behavior

Very cold storage encourages starch to convert to sugars, changing flavor and browning during frying or baking. That is why the refrigerator is not the usual storage place for whole raw potatoes.

Green or heavily sprouted potatoes need different judgment

Light exposure and aging can increase bitter compounds around green areas and sprouts. Discard heavily green, bitter, soft, or badly deteriorated potatoes; refrigeration does not make a damaged potato safe again.

Cooked potatoes should be refrigerated

Once cooked, cool and refrigerate potatoes within two hours, or one hour in very hot conditions, using appropriate containers. Do not leave cooked potatoes at room temperature overnight.

faq.question: What changes once a potato has been cooked?
faq.answer: Once cooked, cool and refrigerate potatoes within two hours, or one hour in very hot conditions, using appropriate containers. Do not leave cooked potatoes at room temperature overnight.
